title: Goldman Sachs: ‘Robust’ live touring and emerging markets fuel $200bn industry forecast
summary: Goldman Sachs has raised its growth forecast for the global music industry for the first time in three years, in part due to the “globalisation of the concert ecosystem” opening up a world of opportunities. With its annual Music In The Air report, the US banking institution projects the industry’s value will rise to nearly $200 billion (€178bn) in the next decade, representing a 5.8% compound annual growth rate (CAGR). By comparison, the industry was valued at $112.5bn (€100bn) in 2025. title: Fatboy Slim, Robbie Williams to lead Isle of Wight’s quarter-century celebration
summary: Fatboy Slim, Robbie Williams, and Kings of Leon are to headline 2027’s Isle of Wight Festival, which will mark a quarter-century since the event’s revival in 2002. title: Languages on The O2 stage triple in eight years
summary: The number of languages represented across performances at London’s The O2 has tripled since 2018 as the demand for global artists explodes. The 20,000-capacity venue is experiencing its most linguistically diverse year yet in 2026, with 18 languages represented across the year — a nearly 30% boost since 2024 alone and 200% from 2018. Languages range from Spanish, Catalan, and French to Korean and Japanese, as well as African ones of Yoruba and Lingala. title: Australian festivals rally to all-time high $400m revenue and attendance in 2025
summary: Despite the Australian festival scene often painted in crisis, the contemporary music festival sector achieved its highest revenue and attendance levels in 2025, hitting nearly A$400 million (€250.3m) and drawing over 2 million people.
